pr.title: feat(ask_user): redesign question cards + batch wizard
pr.body:
Implements OpenSpec change **`redesign-ask-user-question-cards`**.

## Single-question cards (client-only)
- **confirm** — `Yes`/`No` labels (was `Allow`/`Deny`); answered shows **both** options with the pick highlighted.
- **select** — pending: vertical full-width rows, number hotkeys, optional description sub-line (split on `—`/`·`), dashed Cancel row. Answered: full option list dimmed, pick highlighted, **no fold / no `+N more`**.
- **multiselect** — answered shows the full list (checked/unchecked split) with an `X of N` count.
- **input** — answered keeps the question as title, value in a read-only field; empty submit → `(left blank)`.
- New shared `AnsweredCard` shell + `option-text.ts` (`splitOption`/`isCancelOption`).

## Batch as a single-request wizard (client + bridge + shared protocol)
- **shared** — new `ask-user-types.ts` (`batch` method + params/answer/result types).
- **bridge** — `ask-user-tool.ts` dispatches **one** `ctx.ui.batch` request and awaits one `{answers}`; `prompt-bus` type union adds `"batch"`; `bridge.ts` patches `ctx.ui.batch` → PromptBus (questions in `metadata`); new `batch-decode.ts`.
- **client** — new `BatchRenderer` wizard (stepper, Back/Next, Review page with per-row Edit, withhold-until-Submit, multiselect pills, read-only resolved summary); registry `"batch"`; `useMessageHandler` threads `metadata.questions`; `prompt-answer-encoder` batch arm.

Single-method calls (`confirm`/`select`/`multiselect`/`input`) are unchanged on the wire — additive only.

## Verification
- ✅ 163 tests across all touched suites pass (TDD, tests-first per section).
- ✅ `npm run build` succeeds; `tsc --noEmit` clean for all changed files.
- ✅ Docs updated: `file-index-{client,extension,shared}.md` + `architecture.md` (caveman style).
- ⏳ Deferred (task 8.3): `npm run reload` / `POST /api/restart` + live-session manual verification against `mockups/` — needs a running dashboard wired to this worktree.

Pre-existing `pi-image-fit` Jimp test failures are unrelated to this change.
